description: Kurz und knapp Du hast dein Studium in der Tasche, sprühst vor Energie und willst nicht nur zuschauen, sondern echte Verantwortung übernehmen? Bei Picnic startest du direkt in einer Führungsrolle durch! Als Graduate Operations Supervisor (m/w/d) in unserem teilautomatisierten Fulfillment Center (FC) in Falkensee bist du der Motor des Standorts. Unterstützt von Investoren wie der Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation bauen wir gemeinsam das modernste, 100 % elektrische Liefersystem Europas. Du kannst aber schon früher bei uns starten und dein Onboarding an einem unserer bestehenden Standorte absolvieren - zum Beispiel in unserem manuellen Fulfillment Center in Ludwigsfelde oder unserem vollautomatisierten Fulfillment Center in Oberhausen. So bekommst du einen umfassenden Einblick in unsere Operations und bist bestens vorbereitet, wenn wir in Falkensee an den Start gehen. Das erwartet dich  Teamleitung: Du bist Coach und Vorbild – mit deinem echten, intrinsischen Interesse an Menschen führst und inspirierst du dein Team aus 5 Lead Shoppers und über 150 Shoppers. Ownership: Du hast Lust, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, auch wenn Dinge mal außerhalb deines unmittelbaren Bereichs liegen. Du schaust über den Tellerrand hinaus und nimmst die Dinge proaktiv selbst in die Hand. Das bringst du mit Ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor oder Master) in Logistikmanagement, Supply Chain Management, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich. Du brennst für die Logistik und bringst idealerweise erste Einblicke aus dem Lagerbereich mit (z. B. durch Praktika oder ein Werkstudium). Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch & Englisch und bringst die nötige Flexibilität für die Arbeit in zwei Schichten (6:00 – 14:30 Uhr & 14:30 – 23:00 Uhr, auch samstags) mit. Ein extrem hohes Maß an Eigenantrieb. Du siehst Dinge von selbst, nimmst sie proaktiv in die Hand und übernimmst Verantwortung – auch über deinen eigenen Tellerrand hinaus. Ein echtes, intrinsisches Interesse an Menschen. Du bist empathisch, nahbar und liebst es, dein Team zu motivieren und weiterzuentwickeln. Darauf kannst du dich freuen Starte durch - mit uns: Werde Teil unseres internationalen Teams in einem Umfeld, das echtes Wachstum und eine „Act like an Owner“-Mentalität fördert. Bei uns hast du die Chance, Projekte eigenverantwortlich voranzutreiben, neue Ideen zu testen und direkt miterleben zu können, wie deine Arbeit in unserem schnell wachsenden Unternehmen Wirkung zeigt. Nachhaltigkeit als Kern: Werde Teil der Revolution. Du trägst zu einer grüneren Zukunft bei – durch unsere 100 % elektrische Flotte und eine Lieferkette, die Lebensmittelverschwendung reduziert. Die Basics: Wir stellen dir alles für deinen Erfolg bereit – inklusive Laptop und Handy sowie Zugang zu exklusiven Mitarbeiter-Rabatten (Corporate Benefits) für Reisen, Technik und vieles mehr. Zeit zum Auftanken: Mit 30 Urlaubstagen pro Jahr (bei einer 40-Stunden-Woche) sorgst du für den perfekten Ausgleich zwischen Arbeit und Erholung. Verpflegung für Gewinner: Wir kümmern uns um dich. Genieße jeden Tag ein frisches, kostenloses Frühstück, Mittag- und Abendessen in unserem Fulfilment Center, dazu gibt es reichlich Snacks und Obst für den Energiekick zwischendurch. Unvergessliche Momente: Wir sind mehr als nur ein Team. Von unserem legendären jährlichen Ski-Trip über Weihnachtsfeiern bis hin zu Auftritten unserer eigenen Picnic-Band: Wir feiern unsere Erfolge gemeinsam. Individuelle Mobilität:  Du entscheidest, wie du zu uns kommst. Du erhältst einen Firmenwagen (auch zur privaten Nutzung) und kostenlose Parkplätze an den Picnic Standorten stehen dir zur Verfügung. Dazu bieten wir ein „Lease-a-Bike“-Programm an. Lebensmittelretter: Hol dir unsere exklusiven "Too-Good-To-Go"-Tüten und rette leckere Lebensmittel – nur für unsere Mitarbeitenden! title: Data Engineer (m/f/d)
description: At Superchat, we're rebuilding how businesses talk to their customers. The phone call, the contact form, the support ticket: all of it is being replaced by messaging and AI. We're building the platform that runs underneath. Founded in 2020, Superchat has become the platform of choice for 10,000+ businesses worldwide , from globally recognized brands like Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone, and GASAG to the small businesses, dental practices, and one-person startups that need to look bigger than they are. Vor allem als Frau oder als jemand einer unterrepräsentierten Bevölkerungsgruppe. Auch wenn du nicht überall einen Haken setzen kannst, möchten wir dich ermutigen, dich trotzdem zu bewerben. description: Bist du bereit, deine Sales-Karriere in einer der aktuell spannendsten, wachsendsten und beständigsten Branchen zu starten oder auf das nächste Level zu bringen? That's why we've built our own internal support tooling from the ground up, tailored to help our customer, courier, and merchant support teams shine in every interaction. We build high-performance admin applications and core operational tools that empower our support teams to work smarter and faster. A key part of this is our in-house chat platform, which already handles around 5 million conversations every month. On top of this foundation, we're developing advanced features to reduce manual work, improve communication, and proactively resolve issues — often before our users even notice them. Our systems range from automated reach-outs for delayed orders to deeply integrated tools that enable our support teams to deliver assistance quickly, reliably, and with a human touch. By removing inefficiencies and automating repetitive tasks, we're ensuring that our users and partners receive world-class support at scale. About the role We're now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to join us in building scalable, low-latency systems that power these tools and shape the future of customer support. You'll work on impactful products that directly influence how millions of people experience our platform every day. What you'll be doing Build and maintain high-throughput backend services using Go . Collaborate with product managers, designers, and frontend developers to ship features that support internal support agents across the globe. Design systems that are scalable , resilient , and easy to maintain. Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decision-making. Write well-tested code and help the team maintain high code quality standards. Requirements 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a proven track record of building and scaling complex systems. Production experience in Golang , with an interest in developing strong engineering practices. Strong hands-on experience with both SQL and NoSQL databases — especially Cassandra. Solid understanding of designing and operating low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems . Previous on-call experience , with a pragmatic approach to reliability and incident management. Nice to have Background in Node.js or other backend languages. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) and event-driven architectures. Why Deliveroo Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it. We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas. title: Head of Hospitals & Home Care
description: Qui sommes-nous ? Doctolib est une entreprise B Corp engagée à construire ensemble la santé dont nous rêvons tous. Avec 2 900 collaborateurs en France, en Allemagne, en Italie et aux Pays-Bas, nous accompagnons plus de 420 000 professionnels de santé et 90 millions de patients, transformant l'accès aux soins et la prise en charge à travers l'Europe. Nous accélérons désormais notre ambition : devenir le partenaire clinique de référence en Europe, de confiance pour les patients et les professionnels, grâce à la puissance de technologies avancées et de l'IA. Notre ambition est de construire le système d'exploitation clinique de demain pour l'Europe - offrant des résultats de santé mesurables pour des millions de personnes. Pour les professionnels de santé : Nous réduisons la charge administrative, augmentons la prise de décision clinique grâce à l'IA et permettons de nouveaux modèles de soins. Pour les patients : Nous passons de soins réactifs en cas de maladie à une gestion proactive de leur santé, en donnant aux personnes les moyens de prendre en charge leur santé avec des compagnons numériques de confiance, recommandés par les médecins. Vos missions L'hôpital est l'un des segments les plus stratégiques et exigeants de Doctolib. En une décennie, nous avons construit une présence solide auprès des établissements de santé, publics et privés à but non lucratif, avec une suite complète de solutions couvrant l'ensemble du parcours ambulatoire : visibilité de l'offre de soins, planification, prise de rendez-vous, préparation administrative, assistant de consultation IA, téléconsultation, téléexpertise et bien plus encore. En tant que Head of Hospitals & Home Care, vous prenez la tête d'une équipe d'une quinzaine de personnes, structurée en acquisition et account management, et appuyée par de nombreuses équipes expertes partenaires, notamment Déploiement, Interopérabilité, Product Marketing et Affaires Publiques. Vous êtes le ou la garant(e) de la performance commerciale, de la satisfaction client et de la vision stratégique du segment hospitalier en France, tout en ouvrant la voie à de nouveaux territoires : le médico-social et les soins à domicile. Votre responsabilité sera de combiner performance à court terme, développement de la base installée et construction d'une vision stratégique à deux ou trois ans pour le segment. Vous rejoindrez l'équipe Salaried & Retail France de Doctolib, en reportant à Maric Philibert, notre VP Sales, Salaried & Retail. Vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à : Piloter et atteindre les objectifs de net MRR du segment, sur l'acquisition, l'expansion et la rétention, avec une implication personnelle dans le développement des comptes les plus stratégiques et l'accélération du cross-sell sur les nouvelles solutions, notamment l'Assistant de Consultation et la Téléexpertise. Assurer la satisfaction et l'usage effectif des solutions Doctolib dans les établissements clients, en coordination étroite avec les équipes Déploiement, Interopérabilité et Customer Care. Manager, développer et engager une équipe d'environ 15 personnes, accompagner sa montée en séniorité et renforcer son efficacité grâce à la donnée et aux agents IA. Construire et incarner la vision stratégique à deux ou trois ans du segment, en lien avec la Product Vision de Doctolib et les tendances de marché, en coordination avec les équipes Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques, Communication et Produit. Développer et entretenir les relations institutionnelles clés, notamment avec la FHF, la FEHAP, UNICANCER, la DGOS et les ARS, et piloter les partenariats stratégiques du segment. Explorer et initier les premiers revenus dans les segments médico-social et soins à domicile, en définissant les besoins, la stratégie et les approches tactiques adaptées. Développer une approche structurée de segmentation, d'account planning et de couverture des comptes stratégiques, afin d'augmenter l'adoption, l'expansion, le cross-sell et la rétention. Coordonner les équipes Tech, Déploiement, Legal, Finance, Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques et Partenariats, tout en gardant les priorités clients et terrain au centre des décisions. Représenter Doctolib auprès d'interlocuteurs exécutifs, institutionnels, politiques, techniques et des principaux réseaux professionnels du secteur. Votre impact Au cours des 12 premiers mois, vous aurez établi un diagnostic clair et un plan opérationnel pour le segment, renforcé l'équipe et les managers, amélioré la visibilité sur la performance et créé une nouvelle dynamique autour des comptes stratégiques et des opportunités de croissance. À deux à cinq ans, la réussite se traduira notamment par : Faire progresser le revenu et doubler la croissance en new ARR annuel via l’upsell (licences des solutions historiques), le cross sell (livraison de solutions autour de l’IA et de la coordination des soins) ainsi que l’acquisition de nouveaux clients dans les segments hospitaliers sous-exploités aujourd’hui , le médico-social, les EHPAD et les soins à domicile. Profil recherché Nous recherchons un leader senior capable d'agir comme le ou la CEO du segment et d'évoluer avec crédibilité auprès d'interlocuteurs exécutifs internes et externes. Vous justifiez d'une expérience significative auprès d'établissements de santé, acquise comme fournisseur ou prestataire, éditeur e-santé, acteur de la healthtech, dirigeant d'établissement ou de groupe, institutionnel ou consultant en santé avec une forte dimension commerciale. Vous comprenez les acteurs, les personas, les cultures, les rythmes, les circuits de décision et les enjeux politiques et réglementaires du secteur. Vous avez une expérience de la vente B2B complexe et grands comptes, avec des organisations comprenant de nombreuses parties prenantes et des cycles de vente longs. Vous maîtrisez l'acquisition, la vente de solutions complexes, la gestion de comptes stratégiques, l'expansion, l'adoption et la rétention. Vous apportez une vision business 360° couvrant la stratégie, le go-to-market, l'acquisition, l'expansion, les partenariats, le produit, les opérations et l'account management, sans angle mort. Vous avez managé et développé une organisation d'au moins 10 personnes, idéalement composée de profils hétérogènes, avec un historique de transformation, de montée en séniorité et de développement de managers. Vous savez délivrer des résultats à court terme tout en construisant le segment à moyen et long terme, avec rigueur analytique, gravitas C-level et excellente coordination transverse avec Tech, Déploiement, Legal, Finance, Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques et Partenariats. Vous maîtrisez le français et l'anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit. Ce serait un plus si vous aviez aussi : Une expérience des acteurs du médico-social, des EHPAD ou des soins à domicile, ou une forte motivation pour contribuer activement à l'ouverture de ces marchés. Une bonne compréhension des enjeux politiques et réglementaires de la santé numérique, notamment le Ségur du Numérique, l'interopérabilité, les financements publics et les politiques de santé. Une aisance naturelle dans les interactions à dimension institutionnelle ou politique, avec une gravitas adaptée aux interlocuteurs C-level, publics et techniques. Une expérience dans une scale-up, un éditeur e-santé, une direction hospitalière ou de groupe, un acteur institutionnel ou un cabinet de conseil en santé. title: Enterprise Account Executive - EMEA
description: About Abacum Abacum is the leading Business Planning solution for finance teams to drive performance . Founded in 2020 by two former CFOs, we’ve grown into a global team of 100+ people across 30+ nationalities . Headquartered in New York , we have offices in Toronto and Barcelona. We’re trusted by industry leaders such as Dish Networks, Strava, BetterUp, Kajabi, JG Wentworth, Abridge, Cortex , and hundreds more. You've carried a number selling planning, EPM, FP&A or finance software. You know how a CFO buys, how a steering committee stalls, and how to get a multi-stakeholder deal signed. At Abacum you'll own a named territory of enterprise and upper mid-market accounts across EMEA. Many of them run legacy planning tools or spreadsheets that can't keep up with the business. Your job is to show them a better foundation, and win. As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will... - Own the full sales cycle for a named book of enterprise accounts, from first meeting to signed contract - Build and run your own pipeline through targeted outbound, events, and partner co-selling with ERP vendors and implementation partners - Sell to CFOs, VPs of Finance and Heads of FP&A, and bring IT, procurement, security and legal along the way - Run complex evaluations: discovery, business cases, proofs of concept, and competitive displacements - Forecast with discipline and keep a clean pipeline in CRM - Work with Solutions Engineering, Product and Leadership to shape deals, and feed what you hear in the market back into the roadmap What we need... - 6+ years of quota-carrying B2B SaaS sales, with at least 3 years closing enterprise deals - Experience selling EPM, FP&A, planning, or other Office-of-the-CFO software (finance, ERP, spend, or data platforms) - A track record of closing six-figure ARR deals with 3–6 month cycles and hitting or beating quota - Comfort leading multi-stakeholder deals with finance, IT, procurement and security at the table - Experience displacing an incumbent, whether a legacy system or a spreadsheet-based process - A consultative, value-based approach: you build a business case in a CFO's language - The drive to build your own pipeline, not wait for inbound - Clear, sharp written and verbal communication, including running demos with senior buyers - Based in EMEA, with the ability to travel to customers and events Bonus points if you have... - Sold with or through ERP ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics) or implementation partners - Worked in finance, or you're comfortable talking models, drivers and variances with an FP&A team - Used a structured sales method (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or similar) - Been an early seller at a scaling company and helped build the enterprise playbook Why sell Abacum You know the category. Here's why this is the product you want in your bag. 1. A market ready to switch. Finance teams are stuck between rigid legacy planning tools that need a rebuild every time the business changes, and spreadsheets and AI tools no one can trust. Abacum is the governed, AI-native foundation that fixes both. That's a displacement story you can tell in every account. 2. AI that stands up to a CFO. Plenty of vendors claim AI. Ours runs on a governed financial model, so the AI reasons and the math stays exact. CFOs and IT teams can trust the output, and that wins technical evaluations. 3. Faster time to value than legacy EPM. 700+ integrations and self-service data pipelines mean customers see value in weeks, not after a long implementation. That shortens your cycle and makes the business case easy to sign. 4. Channels that bring you deals. Abacum is the only FP&A platform to pass NetSuite's SuiteCloud Developer Network review, is listed on the Sage Intacct Marketplace, and is a verified Microsoft Dynamics 365 partner. Those ecosystems and our implementation partners mean co-sell pipeline, not just cold outbound. 5. A product that keeps getting stronger. New AI skills ship every week. Abacum works where finance already works: Excel, Slack, Claude and ChatGPT, through MCP-native infrastructure. You'll have something new to show every quarter. 6. Funded to win enterprise. Abacum raised a $60M Series B to scale into larger customers. You'll join as we build the enterprise motion, with the room to shape it and grow with it. What you get - Competitive base, uncapped commission, and equity - Remote in EMEA, with hubs in New York, Toronto and Barcelona - Direct access to leadership and a real say in how we sell to enterprise Benefits Competitive compensation including equity package Competitive vacation policy Medical Insurance L&D budget Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform) Language courses (English / Spanish) Our Values Customer Obsession: We share the understanding that Abacum's sole purpose is to create value for customers and relentlessly deploy all creativity and energy to that end. Good People: We are self-reflective and praise diversity of thought. We don't justify the end with the means and know where to draw the line. We have fun every day. Tough Love: We truly care for everyone in the team and embrace honest feedback and radical candor as ways to genuinely help each other. title: Senior Analyst, Permanent Control
description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. Please make your application, including your CV, in English Language . We are a global compliance team headquartered out of London. About the role As a Senior Analyst – Permanent Controls , you will join the Permanent Controls team, a global Second Line of Defence (2LoD) function based across Paris and Mauritius. Reporting directly to the Head of Permanent Controls within the Compliance department, you will focus on the financial perimeter, exercising second-line control, independent oversight, and framework monitoring over the organization's finance domain. You will partner closely with the First Line of Defence (1LoD) to establish control standards, design control matrices, and provide guidance when needed. You will also execute 2LoD control plans, issue formal findings, and track recommendations through to resolution. Sitting in the Second Line of Defense, the global Permanent Controls team serves as an ongoing, trusted advisor and objective challenge to operational teams (1LoD), helping them design robust controls and ensure operational integrity across the organization. Unlike periodic audit functions, Permanent Controls operates continuously to proactively identify vulnerabilities, standardize control frameworks, and foster a strong risk culture. Note on Governance: This is a 2LoD function focused on ongoing control design, execution, and 1LoD enablement. It is distinct and independent from the Internal Audit (3LoD) function within Checkout.com. Key responsibilities Control Design: Collaborate with stakeholders to translate identified risks into comprehensive 2nd line control plans, standards, and templates. 1LoD Enablement: Partner with the First Line of Defence teams to design, refine, and assess their control matrices, ensuring alignment with internal standards and regulators' expectations (ACPR, FCA..). Execution & Testing: Formalize and execute second line permanent controls across critical perimeters, including: Financial regulatory reporting across global entities (France, UK, US, etc.). Accuracy of financial data, accounting standards, and reconciliations. Internal financial processes, procedures, and statutory compliance (including the Order of 3 December 2014). Safeguarding mechanisms (flow of funds, compliance with safeguarding measures, timelines, and incident monitoring). Reporting & Escalation: Present detailed control findings and anomaly reports to the Head of Permanent Controls; track the implementation of remediation recommendations. Proactive Continuous Improvement: Identify operational control gaps, take the initiative to propose practical solutions, and drive improvements to the overall control framework. Tooling & Automation: Contribute to the implementation and optimization of automated control tools, tracking dashboards, and recommendation monitoring systems whenever possible. About You Experience: 5 years of experience in Financial Audit, Internal Control, or Financial Reporting within the financial services (banking, Fintech..) or payments industry. Regulatory Context: Familiarity with regulatory frameworks and ACPR expectations is strongly preferred. Mindset & Working Style: Proactive & Autonomous: A "go-getter" who takes ownership, anticipates control gaps, and brings actionable solutions to the table rather than waiting for direction. Naturally Curious: A drive to understand end-to-end business operations, data flows, and complex payment mechanics. Rigorous & Analytical: Meticulous attention to detail with an ability to leverage data analytics to evaluate controls, transactions and processes objectively. Languages: Fluency in French and English is required. Communication: Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate clear findings and influence decision-making across lines of defence. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? title: Network Operation Engineer
description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed. Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift. Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far. 3. Who we're looking for A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for. Must-have Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong. Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told. Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge. Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus. Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you. Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher. Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly. Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time. Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day. Nice-to-have CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE. Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience. Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs. Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar). Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI). Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry. Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network. Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation. IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene). 4. What we offer A seat inside a serious, very senior network team , with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions. A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build. Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday. Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits , fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet. title: Network Developer
description: Senior Network Developer About Share Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served. The Role Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices. You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team. What you'll do Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time. Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist. Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable. Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change. Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop. Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system. Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off. Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you. Our Ideal Candidate 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP. Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit. Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense. Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you. You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe. You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed. AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't. You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network. A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders. Nice to have Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale. Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them. Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling. 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification. Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it. Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America. DDoS mitigation at the edge. If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway. title: Network Operation Engineer
description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed. Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift. Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far. 3. Who we're looking for A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for. Must-have Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong. Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told. Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge. Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus. Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you. Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher. Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly. Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time. Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day. Nice-to-have CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE. Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience. Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs. Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar). Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI). Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry. Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network. Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation. IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene). 4. What we offer A seat inside a serious, very senior network team , with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions. A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build. Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday. Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits , fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet. title: AI Technical Lead - Developer Tooling
description: AI is fundamentally changing how developers write, understand, debug, and maintain software. At JetBrains, we're exploring what an AI-native development experience should look like for C++ developers. We are looking for a senior technical leader to help shape this future by building AI-powered workflows, integrating coding agents into developer tools, and defining how CLion can become a first-class environment for AI-assisted software development. This is a highly hands-on role focused on technical leadership rather than people management. You should expect to spend most of your time prototyping, implementing, and validating AI-powered workflows while helping shape technical direction through hands-on engineering. You'll work at the intersection of developer tools, AI agents, IDE architecture, and product strategy while helping define how software developers work with AI in the future. Example problems you'll work on: How can coding agents become more effective when working with large C++ codebases? How can CLion's debugging, code understanding, and navigation capabilities be integrated into AI-assisted development workflows? How should AI-powered developer experiences be evaluated and benchmarked in real-world development scenarios? What capabilities should AI agents have access to inside a modern IDE? How can we make CLion a better environment for developers who increasingly collaborate with AI tools and agents? In this role, you will: Shape and deliver AI-powered features for CLion and C++ development workflows. Design the architecture for AI integrations, agent tools, and C++-specific AI capabilities. Build practical benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for AI-assisted C++ development scenarios. Prototype and validate new AI workflows, including debugging, code understanding, refactoring, and project navigation. Collaborate with product managers, ML engineers, QA engineers, stakeholders, and senior developers to shape and deliver the roadmap. Work closely with JetBrains AI, ML, and product teams to help define the AI strategy for the C++ ecosystem. Evaluate and prioritize AI initiatives, bringing new ideas and proposals that align with the broader JetBrains AI strategy. Contribute hands-on to technical design, software architecture, and implementation in a large, mature codebase. Help define a technical roadmap for AI agent and tool integrations in C++ development workflows. Build trust and alignment across the C++ Ecosystem, AI, Product, QA, and ML organizations We'd love to talk if you have:  Significant software engineering experience as a Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, Technical Lead, or similar senior technical role. Strong experience with Kotlin, Java, or other JVM technologies, or the ability to quickly become productive in a JVM-based codebase. Experience building AI-powered products, developer tools, coding assistants, agents, or LLM-based workflows. Strong understanding of how modern coding agents operate, including tool calling, context management, MCP, and evaluation techniques. A track record of driving technical direction in ambiguous and rapidly evolving areas. Strong product instincts and an ability to balance innovation with practical delivery. Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence without formal authority. Nice to have Experience with C++ development workflows, compilers, debuggers, language tooling, or developer productivity products. Experience with IDE internals, language servers, code analysis, refactoring systems, or static analysis. Experience leading small teams or acting as a technical lead. Experience working on AI-native developer products. Why this role is unique Rather than building generic chat experiences, you'll be working on challenges such as AI-assisted debugging, agent-powered code understanding, developer workflow automation, and evaluation systems for AI-powered development tools. Your work will directly influence products used by millions of developers worldwide and help shape JetBrains' broader vision for AI-powered software development. title: Full Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description: TL;DR Join GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology. We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than "implement what's in the ticket". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked. We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them. The problem we're solving Large organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting. GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow. Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems. What we're looking for You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like "customers need a better way to manage X". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here. You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions. You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached. You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them. You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere. You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence. You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents. You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to. What you'll do Over your first year: Enterprise integrations: into our customers' systems, data, identity providers, and workflows. This is what turns GlassDollar from software somebody logs into, into infrastructure their organisation operates on. APIs and MCP: public REST APIs and MCP servers for our customers, their engineers, and increasingly their AI agents. The interesting part isn't exposing endpoints, it's designing an external platform we'll still be happy supporting years from now. AI inside real workflows: embeddings, vector search, and LLMs across a large database of startups and corporate innovation data. We're less interested in adding a ✨ button to everything than in finding places where AI removes real work. Workflow automation: triggers, notifications, and automation that replace humans moving information between systems. Core product engineering: React interfaces, APIs, PostgreSQL queries, permissions, migrations, performance work, and the occasional bug whose root cause makes everybody stare silently at their screen. Our stack Frontend: TypeScript, React, Material UI, Apollo Client, Playwright Backend: Node.js, GraphQL, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Jest Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Sentry Increasingly: LLM APIs, embeddings, vector search, MCP, AI-assisted engineering workflows You don't need experience with every item. Reasoning about systems matters more to us than having memorised our exact stack. Requirements Substantial production experience with TypeScript, React, and Node.js Comfortable reasoning about relational databases, not just the ORM Can independently take a feature from unclear starting point to production Can read unfamiliar code without immediately proposing a rewrite Nice to have: Experience with GraphQL, Prisma, or PostgreSQL at scale Exposure to LLM APIs, embeddings, or vector search Experience owning systems, not just features Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We'd rather have the conversation than lose someone over a bullet point. How we hire How we work We're a small engineering team, so there are fewer places for responsibility to disappear and no chain of five people between you and a decision. We prefer written context over meetings the calendar invented, and working software over elaborate process. Quickly doesn't mean carelessly. Sometimes the fastest route is the simple version today, sometimes it's another day on a foundation twenty future features will sit on. Knowing which situation you're in is part of the job. Expect to ship to production very early. How we hire No seven-stage endurance test. No algorithm trivia disconnected from the work. Intro. You, us, and whether this is the environment you're actually looking for. Technical conversation. We go deep on something difficult you've built: the decisions, the alternatives, what you'd do differently now. Technical assessment. Usually live coding on a realistic problem, sometimes a small proof of concept instead. We care how you think, not whether your solution matches ours. Offer. If there's strong mutual conviction, we move. One last thing Job descriptions have a habit of producing candidates who optimise themselves against bullet points. Please don't. If you're reading this thinking "I can do most of this, but I haven't worked with MCP", apply. Strong fundamentals, meaningful software shipped, and a bias toward ownership are what we're looking for. The rest is learnable. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Associate Product Owner

Unsere Software hilft dabei, Prozesse effizienter zu machen, neue Geschäftsmodelle zu ermöglichen und unseren Redaktionen den Rücken freizuhalten – damit sie sich auf das konzentrieren können, was sie am besten können: hochwertigen Journalismus! Als dritter interner Entwickler bzw. dritte interne Entwicklerin übernimmst du eine zentrale Rolle in unserem Tech-Team. Du arbeitest an der gesamten Entwicklungskette: von der ersten Idee über Konzeption und Umsetzung bis zu Deployment, Betrieb und Weiterentwicklung. Dabei geht es nicht nur darum, Features zu programmieren. Du hilfst uns, die richtigen Probleme zu erkennen, Anforderungen zu schärfen und Lösungen zu entwickeln, die für unser Business, unsere Nutzerinnen und Nutzer und unsere Redaktionen wirklich einen Unterschied machen. Deine Aufgaben Du konzipierst, entwickelst und betreust unsere Webanwendungen, APIs und Apps. Du arbeitest an unseren Statamic -basierten Plattformen und entwickelst unser CMS weiter. Du entwickelst neue Funktionen mit unserem bestehenden Tech-Stack und verbesserst bestehende Lösungen kontinuierlich. Du beschäftigst dich mit dem Einsatz und der Optimierung von Large Language Models und Coding Agents – zur Automatisierung interner Prozesse und für neue Produktfeatures. Du entwickelst und integrierst RESTful APIs, zum Beispiel zur Anbindung von Systemen wie ActiveCampaign . Du wirkst bei der Konfiguration, Wartung und Absicherung unserer Linux-Server und Deployment -Prozesse mit. Du übersetzt Anforderungen aus unterschiedlichen Bereichen in klare technische Lösungen. Du bringst Struktur in komplexe oder noch nicht vollständig definierte Aufgaben und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen umsetzbare Produkte werden. Du arbeitest eng mit Stakeholdern, Produktverantwortlichen, Redaktion und Geschäftsführung zusammen. Unser Tech-Stack - Wir arbeiten unter anderem mit: PHP und Laravel Statamic PostgreSQL Livewire HTML, CSS und JavaScript RESTful APIs Linux-Servern und modernen Deployment -Prozessen Large Language Models und Coding Agents Du musst unseren Tech-Stack nicht bereits vollständig beherrschen – wichtiger sind uns dein technisches Verständnis, deine Kommunikationsstärke und deine Fähigkeit, komplexe Anforderungen schnell in gute Lösungen zu übersetzen. Du solltest aber Lust haben, mit unseren Technologien zu arbeiten und dich schnell in neue Systeme und Themen einzuarbeiten. Wir suchen keine Person, die jedes Tool schon einmal eingesetzt hat, sondern jemanden, der gute technische Entscheidungen trifft, Zusammenhänge versteht und Verantwortung übernimmt. Qualifikation Du hast fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und beherrschst mindestens eine relevante Programmiersprache sicher. Du hast idealerweise Erfahrung mit Webanwendungen, APIs und Datenbanken. Du interessierst dich für unseren Tech-Stack und hast Lust, dich in Laravel , Statamic , PostgreSQL und Livewire einzuarbeiten oder darin weiterzuentwickeln. Du verstehst, wie man LLMs und Coding Agents sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll in der Softwareentwicklung einsetzt – oder möchtest es lernen. Du kennst dich mit Linux-Servern, Deployment und grundlegenden Fragen der IT-Sicherheit aus oder bist bereit, dich in diese Themen einzuarbeiten. Du kannst komplexe Probleme schnell erfassen, priorisieren und in konkrete nächste Schritte übersetzen. Du kommunizierst klar und gerne – auch mit Menschen, die nicht technisch arbeiten. Du kannst unterschiedliche Anforderungen und Perspektiven zusammenbringen und sicher mit Stakeholdern umgehen. Du arbeitest selbstständig, zuverlässig und lösungsorientiert. Du behältst auch dann den Überblick, wenn Anforderungen sich verändern, Informationen zunächst unvollständig sind oder mehrere Themen gleichzeitig auf dem Tisch liegen. Du hast Freude daran, in solchen Situationen Ruhe, Struktur und Verbindlichkeit zu schaffen. Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sind für die Kommunikation im Team und mit unseren Stakeholdern unerlässlich. Was uns wichtig ist Wir entwickeln nicht zum Selbstzweck. Unser Ziel ist Software, die unmittelbar Wirkung entfaltet: für unser Geschäft, für die Vervielfachung unserer Lizenzen und für unsere Redaktionen, die täglich anspruchsvolle Inhalte produzieren. Dafür suchen wir eine Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Fragen stellt und sich aktiv einbringt. Du solltest dich in einem meinungsstarken, dynamischen Umfeld wohlfühlen, unterschiedliche Perspektiven aushalten und deine eigenen Ideen überzeugend vertreten können. Gleichzeitig ist uns wichtig, dass du pragmatisch bleibst und gemeinsam mit anderen zu guten Lösungen kommst. Benefits Wir bieten dir: Eine Schlüsselposition in einem innovativen und wachstumsstarken Medienunternehmen Die Möglichkeit, unseren Tech-Stack aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln Viel Eigenverantwortung und kurze Entscheidungswege Einen vielseitigen Job mit direktem Einfluss auf unser Business und unsere Produkte Eine unbefristete Festanstellung in Teilzeit oder Vollzeit 28 Tage Urlaub Flexibilität bei Arbeitszeit und Arbeitsort > Drei Tage pro Woche in unserem Büro in Berlin-Mitte, zwei Tage im MobileOffice Persönliche und fachliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einer echten Wachstumskultur Eine offene, freundliche Atmosphäre mit Partnerinnen, Partnern und Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus der ganzen Welt Deine Bewerbung Wir freuen uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und ein kurzes, persönliches Motivationsschreiben mit maximal 1.000 Zeichen: Warum möchtest du als Full Stack Product Developer (m/w/d) bei Table.Briefings arbeiten? Uns interessiert besonders, welche Probleme du gerne löst, wie du mit unterschiedlichen Anforderungen umgehst und was dich daran reizt, Technologie mit konkretem unternehmerischem und redaktionellem Nutzen zu entwickeln. title: Senior Odoo Engineer ERP & E-Commerce (all genders)
description: Introduction Do you want to do more than just maintain an ERP system—do you want to help shape its future? As a Senior Odoo Engineer for ERP & E-Commerce (all genders), you’ll take responsibility for our Odoo platform—the system that powers sales, order processing, logistics, and accounting. You’ll further develop our in-house modules, continue the migration to the Odoo standard, integrate new countries, standardize payment processes, and build our new online store—ensuring it’s fully upgradeable, with streamlined workflows and genuine creative freedom. Your mission The focus is on further developing our Odoo platform—which includes approximately 25 in-house modules—and upgrading it to the target version. In doing so, you’ll rely on an upgrade-friendly architecture based on inheritance rather than modifications to the Odoo core Another key focus of your work will be migrating existing processes to the Odoo standard and integrating new countries—including localization, accounting, and country-specific requirements You’ll ensure seamless and efficient payment processes by integrating PSP connections, SEPA direct debit, and PSD2/SCA, and by managing the interfaces with adjacent systems Together with the relevant stakeholders, you’ll implement our new, mobile-friendly website and online store based on Odoo E-Commerce You ensure code quality and testability, document architecture and design decisions, and provide technical guidance to development partners Your profile You have several years of experience in Odoo development with Python and have implemented your own modules from requirements through to go-live You have worked with Odoo Enterprise in production environments—including Odoo.sh—for several years and are proficient with Git in professional development and deployment processes For you, Odoo is not just a configuration tool: ORM, inheritance, Views, and QWeb, access rights, and cron jobs are all part of your skill set—ideally complemented by Odoo E-Commerce You confidently analyze existing software, refactor it strategically, and further develop it with a focus on quality, maintainability, and stability Experience with Odoo upgrades, data migrations, multi-company setups, or integrating payment service providers is a definite plus You work in a structured and independent manner, document clearly, and communicate on an equal footing in German and English Why us? Work Environment & Organization: You enjoy working in our Munich office and value face-to-face interaction with your team. In addition, you can work from home one day a week. You’ll have the freedom to manage your own schedule within the framework of our operational requirements. Workation: Upon agreement, up to 4 weeks of EU workation per year are possible. If you choose Fuerteventura, we’ll also cover your flight, accommodations, and rental car. Freedom & Responsibility: With us, you’ll take on responsibility, actively contribute your ideas, and work in an environment with short decision-making paths and no rigid processes. Modern Office: Look forward to an ergonomic workspace in Munich with a height-adjustable desk, plenty of greenery from plants, an open atmosphere, and short decision-making paths. Attractive Benefits: Monthly deposits to your EmployeeCARD, subsidies for cell phone and internet service, bike leasing, car subscription, retirement savings, and more . Please note: The application process is coordinated centrally by the ValueNet Group. Embracing Diversity Together At ValueNet, we actively promote diversity and equal opportunity. We invite people from all backgrounds to apply—regardless of race, nationality, religion, beliefs, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or disability. Diversity enriches our team and creates space for innovation and shared success. Values that bring us together For ValueNet, sustainability is more than just a word—it is an integral part of our actions, our products, and our services. Enthusiasm, trust, courage, and responsibility shape our culture. We are actively committed to fostering an inclusive environment that respects each individual’s uniqueness and strengthens our shared goals. You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath. You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo. title: Senior Product Data Analyst- Consumer Growth
description: About the team SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way. As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn. We’re looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You’ll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes. You’ll help answer questions such as: Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value? Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation? What drives repeat usage, retention and churn? Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance? How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments? If you’re motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you. What you’ll do Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation . Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics. Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding. Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist. Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics. Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations. Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value. Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact. Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities. Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes. Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted. Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement. You’ll be great for this role if… You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar. You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis. You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value. You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation. You’ve worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them. You’re proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use. You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike. You’re comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence. You’re curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making. You’re comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style. This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.
