title: Full Stack Product Engineer (100% Remote - Germany | UK | Ireland)
description: Build analytics people can trust. Help define what analytics looks like in an AI-first world. Most analytics platforms ask organisations to trade control for insight. For almost 20 years, Matomo has shown there is another way: powerful, transparent and trustworthy analytics that respects privacy, gives organisations ownership of their data, and helps people understand what's happening, make better decisions, and improve their work. More than one million websites use Matomo. That means you'll work on software that is widely used, technically demanding, and close enough to customers that your work has a visible impact. It's a rare opportunity for engineers: solving meaningful, complex product problems while seeing the difference your work makes for customers. We are independent, profitable, and open source. We are not trying to become a smaller copy of Big Tech analytics platforms. We are building a different kind of analytics company: one where privacy, transparency, customer control, and product quality are part of the core product, not marketing claims. This role focuses on Matomo Core, the foundation of our product and the platform our open-source users, cloud customers, and wider plugin ecosystem depend on. If you want unusually high ownership, visible impact, hard product & platform problems, and the opportunity to strengthen a widely used open-source platform , Matomo is worth a serious look. Why this role matters Matomo Core is the foundation of our open-source product, cloud platform, plugins, integrations and customer-facing features. It has evolved over many years and operates across a wide range of environments, use cases and data volumes. Every improvement to Core benefits customers, open-source users, plugin developers and engineering teams across the Matomo ecosystem. We are bringing responsibility for Core into a newly formed European team. You'll help shape how this team works, where it focuses and how it creates the greatest impact across Matomo. As a Product Engineer, you’ll help decide where Core can create the greatest impact. That could mean solving a difficult customer problem, strengthening an existing capability, creating a new platform capability, or simplifying the Core platform to make it easier to evolve. You’ll work on a mature and technically complex product. The challenge is not simply to preserve what exists. It is to understand why it exists, recognise where it is holding customers or engineers back, and evolve it without disrupting the open-source users, customers, integrations and plugins that already depend on it. What you’ll own You'll own problems, not just code. This is not a traditional feature-ticket engineering role. You'll understand customer problems, shape solutions, build across the stack, ship incrementally and continuously improve what you release. AI should be part of your everyday workflow. You'll own work from problem to outcome: Understand the problem before committing to a solution. Help shape priorities, not just implement them. Build across the stack wherever the problem takes you. Ship incrementally and learn from real usage. Measure outcomes and iterate. Use AI throughout your workflow. For senior: You'll help shape what we build, not only how we build it. You'll identify opportunities others haven't seen, influence technical and product direction, and help establish how the Core team operates as it grows. For intermediate: You'll contribute to deciding what we build, working closely with product, engineering and customers rather than simply implementing predefined requirements. You'll own meaningful problems end-to-end while building confidence in navigating ambiguity and product trade-offs. What the work looks like You'll work across the Core platform wherever you can create the greatest impact. Examples include: Diagnosing and solving complex problems across a large, mature codebase. Strengthening the security, performance, scalability, reliability and resilience of Matomo. Protecting the integrity, accuracy and trustworthiness of the data customers rely on. Strengthen capabilities that support increasingly demanding enterprise use cases. Building and evolving APIs and platform capabilities used by Matomo plugins and integrations. Evolving how Matomo handles consent, privacy and responsible data collection. Advancing server-side tracking, data anonymisation and data-health monitoring. Enhancing analytics capabilities such as goals, ecommerce reporting and dashboards. Simplifying complex analytics workflows and making powerful functionality easier to use. Evolving Matomo's design system to create a more consistent and usable product experience. How we work We’re a small team competing with companies many times our size. That means we optimise for impact. We value: Customer problems over technical elegance. Shipping over endless planning. Simple solutions over unnecessary complexity. Ownership over handoffs. Iteration over perfection. Clear writing over excessive meetings. Pragmatic engineering over abstract architecture. AI where it helps us move faster. Measuring outcomes over assuming we were right. We care about high standards, but we do not confuse high standards with slow processes. We would rather ship a small useful improvement, learn from it, and improve it than spend months perfecting something before customers see it. At the same time, changes to Matomo Core can affect a large number of customers, integrations and plugins. You should be able to move pragmatically while recognising when additional investigation, testing or migration planning is necessary. What we’re looking for For senior: You're already operating with a high degree of autonomy. You naturally identify valuable opportunities, make pragmatic decisions in ambiguous situations, and multiply the team's impact through the systems you build, the decisions you influence and the way you approach problems. For intermediate: You're already comfortable delivering software independently and are looking to take greater ownership of customer problems, product decisions and technical direction. You enjoy building products You get motivated by solving customer problems and delivering value, not by technical novelty alone. You care whether people actually use and benefit from what you build. Seeing a feature make a real difference is more rewarding to you than building something technically clever that nobody uses. You naturally ask: What problem are we solving? Who has this problem? Is this the simplest useful solution? How will we know this made things better? What should we do if the data shows we were wrong? You are comfortable with complex, mature systems You do not need every problem to start with a clean architecture or an empty repository. You are comfortable tracing behaviour across an unfamiliar codebase, understanding historical constraints, debugging difficult interactions, and making incremental improvements without unnecessary rewrites. You can balance immediate customer needs with longer-term platform health. You know when to fix the immediate issue, when to address the underlying cause, and when a broader architectural change is justified. You are comfortable across the stack You are happy working wherever the problem takes you: frontend, backend, databases, APIs, product flows, documentation, or customer feedback. Our stack includes PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, Vue.js, and TypeScript. Exact stack experience is useful, but not required. We care more about your ability to learn, reason, ship, and solve meaningful problems. You use AI as part of how you work We make heavy use of AI-assisted development throughout our engineering workflow. You should already be using AI tools regularly or be strongly motivated to do so. We expect Product Engineers to use AI to increase output and quality. AI does not replace your judgment. You remain responsible for product decisions, technical correctness, security, privacy, maintainability, and customer impact. You’ll probably thrive here if You prefer owning outcomes over receiving detailed tickets. You enjoy solving difficult problems in existing systems as well as building new functionality. You can quickly diagnose complex or intermittent bugs. You can move from customer feedback or operational evidence to investigation, product decision and implementation. You care about reliability, performance and data accuracy, not only visible feature work. You can improve a mature codebase without assuming it needs to be rewritten. You use AI tools heavily and are actively improving how you work with them. You are pragmatic: you can make a focused improvement now while recognising when a deeper change is needed. You can explain technical and product trade-offs clearly. You enjoy working across product, engineering, UX, data and customer feedback. You like small teams where your decisions and output visibly matter. below for intermediate only: You're excited to take on increasingly ambiguous problems. You want to grow beyond implementation into shaping products and technical decisions. You may not enjoy this role if You mainly want to work on new greenfield products. You see maintenance, debugging, reliability or performance work as less valuable than feature development. You want a product manager to define most requirements before you start. You are uncomfortable investigating problems where the cause is initially unclear. You prefer replacing existing systems rather than understanding why they work as they do. You measure success mainly by code quality rather than user or business impact. You are uncomfortable using AI as part of your normal engineering workflow. You need a large team, narrow responsibilities, or highly formal processes to be effective. You prefer polishing a solution extensively before showing it to users. You dislike writing proposals, documentation, or product notes. You are uncomfortable balancing speed, backwards compatibility and long-term platform health. Remote work Matomo is a remote company. We work mostly asynchronously and rely heavily on clear written communication. You should be comfortable working independently, documenting your thinking, and collaborating without needing constant meetings. Location 100% remote — Germany, UK or Ireland only. Hiring process Our process is designed to understand how you think, build, communicate, and use AI in realistic product engineering work. The process usually includes: Application → Screening → Online aptitude test → People & Culture interview → Technical skills interview → Final technical interview. We do not expect unpaid multi-day projects. We want to understand how you approach ambiguous problems, make trade-offs, use AI, and ship useful product improvements. Diversity and Inclusion InnoCraft (trading as Matomo) values what makes you unique. We’re an inclusive employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, because diverse perspectives help us build better products. Interested? If you care about solving meaningful customer problems, improving software that people depend on, working with high ownership, and making privacy-friendly analytics more secure, reliable, accurate and useful, we’d like to hear from you. title: Senior Analytics Engineer (Multiple Domains)

title: Design Engineer
description: Mercura ( YC W25 ) helps the companies that build the real world move at software speed, automating the back-office work that runs the $12 trillion industry behind every hospital, school, and power plant. With a team of 16, we're now targeting $10M by the end of 2026 as well as our expansion into the US. About the role You are the second designer here, and you own product surface end to end: you find the problem, decide if it's worth solving, design it, build it, ship it, and then check whether it worked. That last part is the job. Most designers stop at handoff. You won't have one. You'll sit with a German construction supplier watching them fight a spreadsheet, decide which of their five complaints is the real one, and have something in front of them within days. Then you'll open PostHog to find out if it moved anything. We ship fast and polished. If those feel like you, this is the right role for you. What you will be working on Find the real problem. Run your own customer conversations — no PM filter. Distinguish what users ask for from what they need, and be willing to conclude something isn't worth building. Ship it yourself. Design and write the production code. React/TypeScript. You own the result, not a layer of it. Know if it worked. Instrument what you ship. Define the success metric before you build. Kill your own features when the data says so. Set the quality floor. Empty states, loading states, error states, keyboard behaviour, the transition that makes a slow thing feel fast. Nobody is going to catch these for you. Compress the loop. Prototype in whatever gets to a real answer fastest. Speed here means speed to validated user value, not speed to merged PR. What we're looking for Evidence of discovery. You've changed your own mind about what to build because of something a user said or did. You can tell us about a time you were wrong. Evidence of analytics. You've made a product decision from data you instrumented yourself. You know the difference between a metric that moved and a metric that mattered. Taste. You notice when spacing is off, when a flow doesn't communicate, when an interaction feels sluggish — and you fix it without being asked. We'll look at what you've made. Real code shipped to real users. React and TypeScript to production. Not prototypes, not a bootcamp project. Some Python helps; we can teach it. AI as leverage, not as identity. We don't care which tools you use. We care that you've restructured how you work around them and can show us the difference it made. German and English. Our users are almost entirely German-speaking. You'll be in those conversations from week one. How we work In the office, Munich, five days a week. We build in the same room — decisions happen at desks, not in tickets. Relocation support if you're not here yet. High pace, steep learning curve. Most of the team is here well past six. That's not a policy or a number we track, it's what building something this size with sixteen people currently takes, and it's a phase, not a permanent state. If you're optimising for predictable hours right now, this is the wrong role, and that's a completely reasonable thing to be optimising for. This is not the role if you want specs handed to you, you separate "my design work" from "my engineering work," you need a design system before you can start, or your best work needs a slide to explain it. title: Product Manager (f/m/d)
description: Description We are seeking a product manager to own the "what" and "why" of our quantum sensing measurement systems. You turn customer and market needs into clear product requirements that engineering can turn into specifications, and you own the roadmap for the QDm product line, starting with QDm.1. You sit between our customers (foundries, IDMs, OSATs and failure analysis labs) and every engineering discipline, and you make sure we build the right product in the right order. Who we are Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing. Why join us? Picture this: Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide. Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday. Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on. An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you. Still unsure about why joining us? You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before. From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds. What will you do Own the product requirements: gather needs from customers, the field, the market, and internal stakeholders (serviceability, modularity and product configuration, manufacturability, and cost targets), and turn them into clear, prioritized, solution-neutral requirements. Establish our requirements engineering tooling and workflow: select and set up how we capture, trace, and maintain requirements, from customer need through specification to verification, including change control across releases. Structured prioritization: you make trade-offs explicit and back them with reasoning. We hire for demonstrated skill rather than a specific degree; a technical or scientific background is typical. title: Senior Backend Engineer (B2B SaaS Startup)
description: Our Mission Join us in reshaping global trade in a fast-growing startup! We are traide AI – a VC-backed, B2B deep tech startup based in Berlin, using AI to solve one of the most overlooked yet critical challenges in international trade: customs compliance. Our software automates product classification, reduces regulatory errors, and helps customers save up to 83% of their time. Trusted by leading brands like Siemens Healthineers, Koro, and Jack Wolfskin , we've achieved 2 x growth over the past 12 months – and we're just getting started. Your tasks At traide AI, we believe customs specialists deserve smarter, faster workflows and the future of global trade depends on it. As a Senior Backend Engineer , you'll play a pivotal role in builing robust, AI-powered backend services and infrastructure that drives the value creation for our customers. Your main expertise lies in backend technology but you should not be afraid to contribute to other parts of the application. You'll join a tight-knit, VC-backed B2B startup - calm but ambitious - where your ideas shape both product and culture. Product Development Own the end-to-end delivery of new features and improvements in our web application across the whole stack: shaping everything from technical design to production release Write both client-side and server-side code within our well-established codebases Analyse and communicate trade-offs in technical designs in RFC style discussions, drive decisions for your projects Be the backend expert in rotating project teams, give feedback on the contribution of other team members within your area of expertise Cross-functional collaboration Work alongside designers to shape user flows, evaluate feasibility, and improve interfaces and user experience Partner with AI engineers to bring cutting-edge research and prototypes into production-ready features Contribute your perspective to product discussions, helping set direction with both technical and user impact in mind Code quality & technical excellence Set and uphold high standards for code quality, architecture, and best practices within the team Design and maintain robust automated tests to ensure reliability and quality at scale Develop and improve instructions, guardrails and feedback mechanisms for coding agents Select and configure tooling that improves developer experience and keeps our CI/CD pipeline efficient Proactively identify and solve technical challenges before they become blockers Knowledge sharing Share your expertise through code reviews, mentoring, and documentation — helping others level up and ensuring our knowledge grows as the team grows Who we’re looking for You're an experienced engineer who cares deeply about craft, but even more about impact. You love clear thinking over hype, and you're energized by the idea of turning AI research into products people actually use every day. 7+ years of hands-on software engineering experience , ideally building complex products in dynamic environments Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Computer Science or a related discipline Deep proficiency in TypeScript , including advanced type-level programming Familiarity with synchronous and asynchronous communication patterns , HTTP APIs ( REST and GraphQL ), event-driven architecture, and common design patterns. Solid database skills across both relational and non-relational databases such as Postgres and Redis or similar. Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as Google Cloud , and the services that typically come with them. You embrace AI tools in your workflow and are driven to master emerging technologies You champion code quality and drive best practices across the team You thrive in fast-moving environments - seeking opportunities to learn, grow, and both give and receive feedback Strong English skills (C1 or better); German is a plus but not required Curiosity about adjacent fields like DevOps, Security, Frontend development, AI Engineering etc. Our Tech Stack: React & Chakra UI (Component library) GraphQL Node.js & Prisma (ORM) Python & FastAPI & SQLAlchemy Postgres for storage & Redis for caching & messages Terraform / Open Tofu orchestrating Google Cloud Platform Why us? title: AI Product Engineer
description: Das ist kein gewöhnlicher Job. Wir arbeiten an dem, was unsere Gesellschaft zukunftsfähig macht: Bildung. Dafür bauen wir paddy, das Agentic Operating System für Teaching & Learning. Unsere Mission ist es, Lehrkräfte zu entlasten, Lernergebnisse zu verbessern und die Unterrichtsqualität zu steigern. Tausende Lehrkräfte und hunderttausende Lernende nutzen paddy bereits. Mit starken Investoren im Rücken wachsen wir schnell. Unsere Ambition ist es, den europäischen AI-Player für Bildung zu bauen. Als AI Product Engineer übernimmst du Probleme unserer Nutzer End-to-End: vom Verständnis des Problems über Architektur, Backend und Frontend bis zum Deployment. Du prüfst, ob die Lösung im Klassenzimmer wirklich funktioniert. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf AI Engineering: Du baust die agentischen Systeme, die paddy ausmachen, und bringst sie zuverlässig, schnell und bezahlbar in Production. Aufgaben Agentische Systeme bauen: Du entwickelst die Agent-Architektur von paddy weiter. KI in Production betreiben: Mit Evals, Guardrails und AI Observability sorgst du dafür, dass Qualität, Kosten und Latenz unserer KI-Features kein Zufall sind. End-to-End shippen: Du baust Features vom Verständnis des Problems bis zur fertigen Lösung und verantwortest, wie sie im Schulalltag funktionieren. Produktnah arbeiten: Du sprichst mit Lehrkräften, erkennst echte Bedarfe und triffst mit Product und Design Entscheidungen, statt auf Tickets zu warten. Engineering-Bar heben: Testing, Monitoring und saubere Architektur geben dir Geschwindigkeit. Du erkennst Risiken früh und steuerst technische Schulden bewusst. Qualifikation Product-Engineering-Erfahrung: Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung mit digitalen Produkten und echten Nutzer. AI-Engineering-Know-how: Du hast LLM-Features oder agentische Systeme gebaut und in Production betrieben. Du verstehst Modellfehler, RAG, Evals und Vektor-Datenbanken. ML Research ist nicht erforderlich. Technisches Fundament: Du bist sicher in API-Design, Datenmodellen und der Entwicklung über Backend und Frontend hinweg. Ownership und Urteilskraft: Du kommst mit offenen Problemen klar, findest einfache Lösungen für komplexe Fragen und baust Systeme, die im Schulalltag funktionieren. AI-native Arbeitsweise: Du nutzt Coding Agents und moderne AI-Tools selbstverständlich, um deinen Output zu vervielfachen. Sprachen: Fließend Deutsch und sehr gutes Englisch. Unser Tech Stack Full-stack TypeScript: Next.js, Drizzle, Postgres Web: Next.js, Tailwind, Zod Mobile: React Native, Expo, EAS, React Query AI: Vercel AI SDK, promptfoo, LiteLLM, Arize Phoenix, pgVector Infra: DigitalOcean, Scaleway, Open Telekom Cloud, Azure Benefits Sichtbaren Impact: Du arbeitest am wichtigsten Zukunftsthema unserer Gesellschaft, der Bildung. 70.000 bis 100.000 € Bruttojahresgehalt , abhängig von deiner Erfahrung, plus Equity (VSOP). 100 % Remote-Arbeit. Wenn du lieber ins Büro kommst, steht dir unser modernes Office in Bielefeld offen. Großen Gestaltungsspielraum und Ownership sowie direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Foundern und einem starken Product- und Engineering-Team. Ein hohes Budget , solange der Nutzen stimmt. Zeit und Unterstützung für deine Entwicklung , mit Fortbildungsbudget, Coaching und klaren Entwicklungsperspektiven. 30 Urlaubstage und 50 € monatlichen steuerfreien Sachbezug. Regelmäßige Team-Events und Offsites. Starkes Backing durch erfahrene Investoren und Mentoren. The service is already in production; the mission now is to make it the obvious choice for teams running AI applications on Postgres — first-class vector search, painless migrations from RDS / Cloud SQL / self-managed clusters, and the operational quality of a mature managed database. Strong software engineering skills in Go or another backend/systems language, with a willingness to work primarily in Go. Deep knowledge of PostgreSQL internals: MVCC, WAL, replication (physical and logical), vacuum, query planning, extensions, partitioning. Hands-on experience with the surrounding ecosystem: Patroni / Stolon / pg_auto_failover, pgBackRest / WAL-G, pgBouncer / PgCat, logical replication tooling. title: Technical Product Manager
description: About BJAK The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name. Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you. The Role BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it. This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against. Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery. Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back. Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness. Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record. Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears. Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation. What you'll need Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers. Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify. Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control). AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all. Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience. Outcomes Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction Location This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany . title: Senior Key Account Manager
description: Why Verifone For more than 40 years Verifone has established a remarkable record of leadership in the electronic payment technology industry. Verifone has one of the leading electronic payment solutions brands and is one of the largest providers of electronic payment systems worldwide. Verifone has a diverse, dynamic and fast paced work environment in which employees are focused on results and have opportunities to excel. We take pride in the fact that we work with leading retailers, merchants, banks, and third party partners to invent and deliver innovative payments solution around the world. We strive for excellence in our products and services, and are obsessed with customer happiness. Across the globe, Verifone employees are leading the payments industry through experience, innovation, and an ambitious spirit. Whether it’s developing the next platform of secure payment systems or searching for new ways to bring electronic payments to new markets, the team at Verifone is dedicated to the success of our customers, partners and investors. It is this passion for innovation that drives each one of our employees for personal and professional success. Verifone is proudly an in-office work culture as we see immense benefits to career development and business results from our colleagues being physically co-located. Currently, we do allow a hybrid work schedule but we regularly revisit our attendance policy. What's Exciting About The Role To ensure the long-term stability and growth of strategically important international customer relationships, we are hiring a Senior Key Account Manager . Reporting to and working closely with the current Global Account Manager, you will support the operational and strategic management of key accounts, ensuring continuity of customer relationships while developing the expertise required to assume full account responsibility over time.   This role sits within our DACH sales organization led by our Head of DACH, which is responsible for our SMB, Enterprise, Partner, and eCommerce/ mCommerce segments across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Key Responsibilities: Full backup coverage and involvement in the Key Account Manager's day-to-day business   Building in-depth accounts knowledge (contractual status, contacts, commercial history, open topics) to ensure a seamless handover   Maintaining the customer relationships with key contacts at the international companies on an operational and tactical level   Coordinating internal interfaces (Product, Compliance, legal, Onboarding, Helpdesk, IT) to ensure smooth service delivery   Contributing to forecasting, pipeline maintenance in Salesforce, and account reporting   Preparing for and participating in business reviews and escalation calls   Supporting contract negotiations and commercial proposals in coordination with the Global Account Manager   Skills and Experience We Desire Fluency in both German and English, with the ability to communicate effectively in both languages Extensive experience within the payments industry, with strong expertise in payment gateways, acquiring services, and payment terminal solutions. Proven track record in Key Account Management or Relationship Management, ideally within the payments, financial services, or retail sectors. Experience managing complex international customer organizations, including global and multi-market enterprise accounts. Proficiency in Salesforce and/or comparable CRM platforms, with a disciplined approach to account and pipeline management. Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and negotiation skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior decision-makers. Highly organized and self-motivated, with a structured working style, strong attention to detail, and the reliability to ensure seamless customer support and business continuity when acting as a backup. Key Success Criteria Develop a strong understanding of the assigned key accounts and actively manage them in close partnership with the Global Account Manager. Achieve full backup capability for the assigned accounts by the end of the onboarding period, ensuring seamless customer support and continuity. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with all relevant internal stakeholders across Verifone supporting the customer portfolio. Build trusted relationships with key customer stakeholders across commercial, operational, and executive levels. Consistently deliver a high standard of customer service, reflected in positive feedback from customer contacts and stakeholders. Contribute actively to revenue growth opportunities through accurate pipeline management, forecasting, and account planning. Demonstrate increasing ownership of account activities and readiness to assume broader account responsibilities over time. title: Product Designer | SimpleStudy
description: Role: Senior Product Designer Company: SimpleStudy Location: Remote, Europe (preferably Western / continental); relocation to Lisbon possible Job Type: Full-time About SimpleStudy SimpleStudy is an AI exam prep platform that students find and choose for themselves. In some numbers: 1.5M+ students across the UK, Ireland, Brazil, South Africa, and Australia 40–50k new students every week Web, mobile, and desktop apps $4M seed round with investors from Strava, OpenAI, and Meta The traction came fast. Now the company is refounding: rebuilding the brand, the design language, and the product experience from scratch. The product grew like a Jenga tower, one feature on top of another. The job now is to rebuild it as a pyramid. The team is ~30 people, remote with a Lisbon office — lean, product-led, and deliberately not a typical edtech company. You'll report to José, the Founding Designer, and work with him as a partner. José tends to lead early framing and direction. You bring strong craft and take the work to the finish line, in close sync with engineering. You both shape the new design language, and you push back with a better idea when you see one. What you are expected to do: Shape the new design language and brand: design system, rebrand, and the new mobile app. Own the full design process — from an ambiguous problem to a polished, shipped solution. Drive the consumer experience: onboarding, social features, retention, and the learning loop. Work in close sync with engineers and PM, not as a handoff step - polish the implementation together until it feels right. Bring your own initiatives and say "no, but…" when you see a better way. Raise the bar for the whole design team. What you need to succeed: High craft — your visual work is polished and intentional; the details reveal your thinking. Storytelling over process — you take an ambiguous problem, frame it, and make it simple. Your portfolio shows artifacts, not diagrams; it has a point of view. Consumer instinct — you've shipped B2C products that people chose to use. You understand product metrics and use them as input, but you lead with feel and craft. Opinions with backbone — you have a design philosophy, can defend it under pushback, and bring your own initiatives. You don't wait to be told what to build. Energy and curiosity — you're an interesting person with a life outside work, and you leave people energised after a conversation. English — fluent, written and spoken. What would be a plus: A standout specialty: prototyping, illustration, animation, or motion. Experience with social or viral product mechanics. Background at consumer companies like Spotify or Strava. Early-stage or founding designer experience. Comfortable in code: prototyping or polishing the front end. What you get: Build from scratch, at scale — a new design language for a product already used by 1.5M+ students. A strong partner - work closely with José, the Founding Designer (ex-Shopify), with direct access to the founders. Equity — generous stock options, early enough for them to matter. Remote Europe — work from where you choose, with in-person meetups three times a year; relocation support if you want to move to Lisbon. Competitive salary — no fixed budget, flexible. How to apply: A deck or a walkthrough video is fine. Show the work, keep it curated. title: (Junior) Finance Manager (German Speaking) (m/w/d)
description: DEINE ROLLE Zahlen sind für dich kein Selbstzweck, sondern die Grundlage guter Entscheidungen? This is not about adding AI features to an existing roadmap. You’ll own an emerging problem space and identify where agents can create the highest leverage for our customers beyond what Plancraft does today. That means getting close to tradespeople and their businesses, uncovering the problems worth solving, and working with Engineering and UX to turn them into reliable, trustworthy products customers are willing to rely on for real work. You’ll operate across the full product journey: from spending time with tradespeople in the field and deciding which opportunity to pursue, to working with Engineering to understand technical requirements and trade-offs, defining evaluation criteria, shipping to production, and learning from real-world usage. Establish a repeatable AI product operating loop across discovery, evaluation, release gates, monitoring, and iteration. Define and maintain evaluation sets, quality standards, and release criteria for customer-facing AI products, including accuracy, correction rates, latency, and safe rollback conditions. Instrument and monitor AI product performance, using customer behaviour and quality signals to decide what to scale, change, or stop. Demonstrate measurable customer outcomes from AI-powered workflows, including improvements in efficiency, profitability, quote acceptance, capacity utilisation, activation, and retention. Partner across Product and Engineering to manage dependencies, reusable AI experience patterns, mobile and voice input, and handovers between customer workflows. Must-Have Skills 7+ years of product management experience , including at least 2 years owning and shipping AI products in production end-to-end. Strong applied GenAI literacy across LLMs, agents, RAG, and evaluation frameworks — sufficient to understand technical requirements and help evaluate Product, quality, cost, and time-to-market trade-offs together with Engineering. Experience building 0-to-1 AI products or new product areas , from customer discovery and problem definition through production launch and iteration. Experience defining quality and success criteria for AI products , including evaluation metrics, release thresholds, customer outcomes, and post-launch monitoring. Strong customer discovery and product judgment , with the ability to turn complex real-world workflows into focused AI product opportunities. Experience in a fast-moving startup or scale-up environment , with a track record of creating structure, setting priorities, and delivering despite ambiguity. Proven cross-functional ownership , working closely with Engineering and UX from discovery through production and managing dependencies across teams. English at C1 level and German at C2 level. Willingness to stay close to customers and the team , including field discovery with tradespeople and regular presence in Hamburg (approximately one week per month or equivalent). Experience with AI monetisation , including usage-based, credit-based, or hybrid pricing models. Background in B2B SaaS for SMBs, field service, construction, or the trades . You’re excited by AI because of the problems it can solve — not simply because the technology is new. You’re comfortable working closely with engineers, understanding technical requirements and evaluation results, and translating them into sound Product decisions. You want meaningful ownership. You’re comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, narrowing a large opportunity space into the right first wedge, shipping it, learning from real usage, and changing course when the evidence tells you to. The products you build here should change how trades businesses operate — and their adoption, customer value, and commercial impact will be measurable. WHY PLANCRAFT? Tech & Tooling : You’ll receive a MacBook, premium headphones, and everything else you need — from hardware to tools — to be effective in your daily doing. Flexibility : Whether remote, hybrid, abroad or on-site — you work where you’re at your best. Our Hamburg office (with a rooftop terrace) is always open, and you decide each week how often you come in. And if you need a change of scenery, working abroad worldwide up to 2 months is always an option. Recharge : To ensure the needed rest, we offer 30 vacation days per year (based on a 5-day week) plus Dec 24th off. We also subsidize your Urban Sports Club membership and organize internal sport meetups. Mobility : You can lease a "JobRad" (Bike) and get a subsidized "Deutschlandticket" or "BahnCard" for public transport to be supported in your commute. International Environment : We’re becoming more international every month, with team members already in Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, and Austria — which is why English is our internal company language. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. The AI Customer Success function is being built from the ground up, and this role will help define it internationally. As the first Customer Success Manager in this area, you will own the end-to-end post-sale experience for a portfolio of customers that includes some of the world’s most sophisticated cyber threat intelligence teams and investigators, national security agencies, and financial crime teams. Your mandate is not just to manage accounts—you will help establish the playbook, define what success looks like, and drive a product-led growth motion that turns new customers into long-term, expanding partners. Define and track adoption benchmarks across the portfolio—hands-on-keyboard usage, consumption rates, and account-specific success metrics—and surface at-risk accounts before renewal decisions are made. Identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play within 60 days by working backwards from expansion targets, focusing on the one or two use cases most likely to drive consumption across the customer base. Run executive business reviews and QBRs with senior stakeholders at government agencies and financial institutions internationally—building the trust and credibility that turns TRM from a vendor into a mission-critical partner. Partner with ADs on expansion plays, co-own NRR targets, and build the structured path to proving value for every customer with an expiring or at-risk contract. Close the feedback loop between customers and Product—synthesize adoption blockers, feature gaps, and new use-case opportunities into prioritized, actionable input that informs the roadmap. A high level of independence—you set your own agenda, operate without needing constant direction, and ship v1 before you have all the answers. Strong executive presence—you can run a QBR with a senior government stakeholder or financial institution executive and command the room through substance, not just polish. Experience supporting international customers, with the ability to navigate regional, cultural, and time-zone differences. About the Team: This team focuses on TRM’s AI-driven Intel platform, supporting investigators and cyber teams working on complex cases involving cyber threats. This is the first Customer Success hire dedicated to international customers—you will help build the function from the ground up, with high autonomy, direct access to leadership, and meaningful influence on how TRM approaches customer success globally. The broader TRM CS organization operates distributed, not distant—async-first communication through Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions. You will work directly with the Head of Customer Success and Patrick South, CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with international Sales teams and Product. Team Operating Rhythms: As a globally distributed team, members work across multiple time zones. This role will primarily align its working hours and customer coverage with international markets, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed. Our Customer Success team is fully remote, thriving on asynchronous communication and collaboration through Slack channels and detailed documentation. We hold weekly customer syncs, biweekly health syncs, join our associated POD calls, and regularly engage with customers across international markets. As experts in our craft, we focus on providing support, driving value, and building meaningful relationships with our customers as trusted advisors. We are on the front lines of TRM, ensuring our customers get the most out of the product and bringing valuable insights back to the team. The team moves fast and iterates—v1 ships before it is perfect, and feedback is expected to be direct and specific. On-Call Responsibilities: End-to-End Ownership: While there is no formal hourly rotation, you will be the primary lead for your area and responsible for customer success across international markets. This requires a high degree of agency and a commitment to seeing mission-critical tasks through to resolution, including the flexibility to handle urgent needs outside of standard hours or on weekends when they arise. Learn about TRM Speed in this position: Within 30 days of joining, you ship a working v1 onboarding playbook built from your first 2–3 accounts—not a slide deck, but a live document with measurable adoption benchmarks that the account team is already using to set customer expectations. Within 6 weeks, you share a draft success-metrics framework at 50% complete with the account team and key customers to validate direction—getting real signal on what drives credit consumption before investing further in building out the full playbook. Within 60 days, you identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play by working backwards from expansion targets—presenting a concrete recommendation to leadership on which use case to prioritize and why, grounded in actual account data from international customers. title: Field Application Engineer
description: About Us Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world. The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. Role Summary The Field Application Engineer (FAE) is a hands-on, vehicle system-level role. You will work directly on prototype vehicles and lab cars to investigate complex, cross-subsystem issues, capturing the data needed to reproduce and isolate them. You will also provide diagnostic and integration support on-site at partner facilities. The focus is on getting close to the hardware and the buses, producing clear findings that development teams can act on. This role is based in our Berlin office and requires a minimum of three days per week onsite, with occasional travel to other company and partner sites as needed. Responsibilities Perform hands-on diagnostics on prototype vehicles, including capturing network traces (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and real-time data logs from ECUs and zonal controllers. Work at the vehicle system level to reproduce, characterize, and isolate reported issues across interacting subsystems. Set up and operate measurement and diagnostic equipment to gather ground-truth data directly from the vehicle. Run first-pass triage of field-reported symptoms to help distinguish software defects from environmental or hardware issues. Reproduce and characterize reported issues on target vehicles and test benches.. Document technical findings, logs, and reproduction steps into clear hand-off reports for development teams. Log and update technical tickets in Jira, keeping status and evidence current.. Travel to customer / partner sites, both domestically and internationally, for on-site diagnostics and integration support. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience. Foundational understanding of automotive network protocols (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and willingness to deepen it quickly. Hands-on experience with bus-monitoring / diagnostic tools (e.g., Vector CANalyzer, PCAN, or equivalent) — required. Basic understanding of embedded systems and embedded operating systems. Scripting/programming ability (Python and/or C/C++) for log processing and data capture. Experience working within a CI/CD environment. Experience working with and developing within git. Comfortable working hands-on with hardware in a lab or vehicle environment.. Fluency in English required. Total Rewards We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. Logistics is absolutely integral to Wolt, and doing it well can mean the difference between delivering blissful customer experiences efficiently and profitably vs. operational nightmares and a cacophony of late deliveries. The Delivery Promise team is in the Courier & Logistics Product group at Wolt. We're driving the future with estimates that fuel our growth, flywheel, shaping shopping decisions and streamlining deliveries. Our goal: boost Wolt's growth and profitability by delivering reliable, precise time estimates to customers and partners worldwide. Your Mission Master the General Ledger: Du führst und stimmst die Hauptbücher eigenverantwortlich für ausgewählte Gesellschaften ab und garantierst eine lückenlose, rechtssichere Buchführung nach HGB. Drive financial closings: Du treibst die Erstellung von Monats- und Jahresabschlüssen proaktiv voran und agierst als kompetente Schnittstelle bei Audits sowie steuerlichen Prüfungen. Optimize data & automation: Du sicherst die Datenqualität zwischen operativen Subsystemen und dem Hauptbuch und hebst durch gezielte Kontrollen neue Automatisierungspotenziale. Manage complex structures: Du betreust komplexe Finanzinstrumente und treibst Sonderprojekte, wie beispielsweise die Bilanzierung von ABS-Strukturen oder Forderungsverkäufen, erfolgreich voran. Streamline intercompany workflows: Du verantwortest die reibungslose Abstimmung und Verrechnung zwischen unseren Gesellschaften und etablierst effiziente, konzernweite Finanzprozesse. Ensure compliance & guidelines: Du stellst die strikte Einhaltung gesetzlicher Vorschriften sowie unserer internen Richtlinien sicher und agierst als verlässlicher Sparringspartner im Team. Your Profile Must have: Fundierte Accounting-Expertise: Langjährige, praxiserprobte Berufserfahrung in der Hauptbuchhaltung (General Ledger), idealerweise erworben in einem dynamischen Finanzdienstleistungs-, Fintech- oder Scale-up-Umfeld. Starke HGB- & Sonderstruktur-Kenntnisse: Fundiertes Fachwissen in der Bilanzierung nach HGB sowie nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Betreuung komplexer Finanzinstrumente (z. B. Lösungsorientierte Kommunikationsstärke: Ausgeprägter Teamgeist und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Sachverhalte präzise zu vermitteln – auf Deutsch (min. B2) sowie mit guten, sicheren Englischkenntnissen. Nice to have: IFRS-Kenntnisse: Erste praktische Berührungspunkte oder fundierte Kenntnisse in der internationalen Bilanzierung nach IFRS. Prozessautomatisierung: Erfahrung in der engen Zusammenarbeit mit Product- oder Tech-Teams zur Automatisierung von Schnittstellen und Finanz-Subsystemen. Mit deinem jährlichen Development-Budget in Höhe von 1.500€ für Fortbildungen und Seminare entscheidest du selbst, wie du dich persönlich und professionell weiterentwickelst. Bei Picnic suchen wir nicht nur jemanden, der Prozesse steuert, sondern eine Führungskraft, die ihr Team inspiriert und jeden Tag zu einem Erfolgserlebnis macht. Du coachst, motivierst und unterstützt dein Team aus Shoppers, stellst sicher, dass sie sich wohlfühlen und gemeinsam Großes leisten. Teamwork: Gemeinsam mit anderen Teamleitungen und der Schichtleitung steuerst du proaktiv die Prozesse im FC. Du trägst maßgeblich zu einer positiven und unterstützenden Arbeitsatmosphäre bei. Dabei bist du der Fels in der Brandung, der auch in stressigen Situationen einen kühlen Kopf bewahrt und Ruhe ausstrahlt. Prozessoptimierung: Bringe deine Ideen ein und verbessere gemeinsam mit dem Leadership stetig unsere Logistikprozesse. Du ermutigst dein Team, mitzudenken und sich aktiv einzubringen. Alternativ bringst du min. 1 Jahr Berufserfahrung in der Teamleitung oder einer ähnlichen Führungsposition in der Logistik mit. Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und hast gute Englischkenntnisse, um dich in unserem internationalen Team zu verständigen. Du bist flexibel für die Arbeit in zwei Schichten (6:00 – 14:30 Uhr & 14:30 – 23:00 Uhr, auch samstags) in einer 37,5-Stunden-Woche. Du liebst es, mit Menschen zusammenzuarbeiten und packst selbst mit an. Darauf kannst du dich freuen Starte durch - mit uns: Werde Teil unseres internationalen Teams in einem Umfeld, das echtes Wachstum und eine „Act like an Owner“-Mentalität fördert. Bei uns hast du die Chance, neue Ideen zu testen und direkt miterleben zu können, wie deine Arbeit in unserem schnell wachsenden Unternehmen Wirkung zeigt. Nachhaltigkeit als Kern: Werde Teil der Revolution. Du trägst zu einer grüneren Zukunft bei – durch unsere 100 % elektrische Flotte und eine Lieferkette, die Lebensmittelverschwendung reduziert. Zeit zum Auftanken: Mit 30 Urlaubstagen pro Jahr sorgst du für den perfekten Ausgleich zwischen Arbeit und Erholung. Verpflegung für Gewinner: Wir kümmern uns um dich. Genieße jeden Tag ein frisches, kostenloses Frühstück, Mittag- und Abendessen in unserem Fulfilment Center, dazu gibt es reichlich Snacks und Obst für den Energiekick zwischendurch. Unvergessliche Momente: Wir sind mehr als nur ein Team. Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week. That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works. You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win. — Grigory Why Secfix exists Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it. Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months. We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market. This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more. What you'll actually do in the first 3 months This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes: Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions. Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI. Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews. What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months? After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run. You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game. Here's what you'll be close to in the next months: Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it. Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20. Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager. AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff. What success looks like At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth. How we work We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture. Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture ; give it a read. To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year: Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution. AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here . Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product. We build what customers need , not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us. This role is for you if: You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you. You know what great engineers look like. They're the ones who can frame a problem, write a spec, sit with engineers through the build, and own that what shipped is what they designed. Our founding product designer, Ghada , has been doing exactly that since we started. The engineering team has doubled, and we're shipping faster than we ever have. We're hiring the third designer because there's more good work to do than two people can handle — and we'd rather ship faster than slow down. Why Secfix exists Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. What we believe Compliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm. Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work. What the role is We expect strong design skills, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end. Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster: Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast. Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked. Customer conversations, problem framing, Figma, spec, engineer pairing, PR review, production verification. Month 3 and beyond. Push the design system forward. Start building the tools and skills that make engineers faster at design. Improve the product design process. The bar is yours to defend. Who you are 8+ years designing B2B SaaS desktop applications as Staff/Principal Product Designer or similar. Dense interfaces — tables, filters, permissions, settings pages. title: Operations Manager (m/w/d) | Coaching & Organisation
description: Du bist der Mensch, bei dem am Ende einfach alles läuft . Du liebst Struktur, behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Aufgaben den Überblick und willst einen eigenen Verantwortungsbereich, auf den sich Kunden und Kollegen zu 100 % verlassen können. Dann könnte das hier ziemlich gut zu dir passen. RWKMP® ist eine etablierte Unternehmensberatung aus Münster. Wir begleiten jedes Jahr mehrere hundert Verkäufer und Führungskräfte aus der Automobilbranche in unseren zwölfmonatigen Coachingprogrammen – mit Kunden in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz. Damit diese Programme funktionieren, braucht es hinter den Kulissen perfekte Organisation: Teilnehmer, Termine, Zugänge, Unterlagen, Kommunikation und Live-Trainings müssen zuverlässig ineinandergreifen. Genau dafür suchen wir dich. Dabei arbeitest du nicht mit Zettelwirtschaft und veralteten Systemen. Wir arbeiten digital, nutzen Airtable, Learning Suite, CARvinci, Excel und KI-Tools – und entwickeln unsere Abläufe kontinuierlich weiter. Aufgaben Fünf Bereiche, ein Ziel: Unsere Kunden sollen merken, dass bei uns alles organisiert ist. Kunden & Teilnehmer sauber onboarden – Ein Autohaus startet mit unserem Coaching. Ab diesem Moment sorgst du dafür, dass organisatorisch alles steht: Teilnehmer anlegen, Gruppen zuordnen, Termine verschicken, WhatsApp-Gruppen vorbereiten sowie Zugänge zu Learning Suite, CARvinci und Persönlichkeitsanalysen koordinieren. Der Kunde soll nicht hinter Informationen herlaufen müssen. Zwölf Monate Coaching im Blick behalten – Unsere Programme laufen über ein Jahr. Teilnehmer wechseln, Termine stehen an, Informationen müssen raus und Unterlagen rechtzeitig bereitliegen. Du behältst Gruppen, Termine, Zugänge, Teilnehmerwechsel, Zertifikate und offene Punkte im Blick – und sorgst dafür, dass nichts verloren geht. Prozesse zuverlässig ausführen und verbessern – Du arbeitest nach bestehenden Abläufen, dokumentierst sauber und stellst sicher, dass Prozesse zuverlässig eingehalten werden. Gleichzeitig sollst du mitdenken: Wo entsteht unnötige Handarbeit? Wo passieren Fehler? Was können wir einfacher oder digitaler lösen? Du arbeitest unter anderem mit Airtable, Excel, Learning Suite, ChatGPT und weiteren digitalen Tools . Live-Trainings vorbereiten – In Münster organisierst du gemeinsam mit dem Team unsere Live-Coachings: Teilnehmerlisten, Namensschilder, Unterlagen, Analysen, Raum und Technik. Und du packst selbst mit an. Du kennst unsere Kunden dadurch nicht nur aus einer Datenbank, sondern siehst direkt, was deine Arbeit möglich macht. Digitalisierung mitlernen und mitgestalten – Du musst heute kein Automatisierungs- oder KI-Profi sein. Aber du solltest Lust darauf haben, neue Tools kennenzulernen und gemeinsam mit uns zu überlegen, wie Prozesse noch besser funktionieren können. Wenn du irgendwann selbst einfache Automatisierungen baust oder Abläufe digital weiterentwickelst: umso besser. Du musst weder verkaufen noch selbst Coachings geben. – Dein Schwerpunkt ist klar: Du hältst unsere Coachingorganisation zuverlässig zusammen. Wenn du sagst, dass etwas erledigt ist, möchten wir uns darauf verlassen können, dass es erledigt ist. Du musst weder verkaufen noch selbst Coachings geben. Dein Schwerpunkt ist klar: Du hältst unsere Coachingorganisation zuverlässig zusammen. Wenn du sagst, dass etwas erledigt ist, möchten wir uns darauf verlassen können, dass es erledigt ist. Am Anfang lernst du unsere Abläufe kennen und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt die Verantwortung dafür. Danach kannst du dich fachlich weiterentwickeln: mehr Prozessverantwortung, eigene Projekte, stärkere Digitalisierung oder zusätzliche Verantwortung innerhalb unserer Operations. Außergewöhnliche Struktur – Du behältst mehrere Programme, Teilnehmer, Termine und offene Punkte gleichzeitig im Blick und verlässt dich dabei nicht nur auf dein Gedächtnis. **Zuverlässigkeit & Prozessdisziplin** – Du arbeitest sorgfältig, hältst Zusagen nach und prüfst, ob Dinge wirklich abgeschlossen sind. Fehler versuchst du zu erkennen, bevor sie beim Kunden ankommen. **Excel & digitale Affinität** – Excel oder Google Sheets gehören für dich zum normalen Arbeitsalltag. title: Product Engineer Procurement
description: Job Description ✨ A little about us Container xChange is building the distribution channel for global container trading . We operate in a huge, fragmented and still highly inefficient market. Our ambition is to make it dramatically easier to access the right inventory, compare opportunities, transact and fulfil container purchases across sellers and locations globally. To win, we need to get a few things exceptionally right: more of the right containers, in the right locations, at better prices — from sellers who are fast, reliable and easy to trade with. That is where you come in. 🧭 The Role As Product Engineer – Procurement , you will own our Procurement function end-to-end in close collaboration with our CEO Christian . This is a hands-on commercial builder role: you run Procurement, improve the economics, and build the processes, automations and product solutions that make the function scale. You will start hands-on: run day-to-day procurement, work directly with sellers, negotiate prices and promotions, support Sales on supply opportunities and understand where our current processes work well — and where they break. But your mandate goes further: Build a Procurement function that becomes a competitive advantage for xChange. We want you to constantly ask: How can we improve the economics? How can we make this process faster? What can we standardize? What can we automate? You will use Claude and other tools to build lightweight solutions yourself, experiment with deterministic and agentic automation, and work closely with Engineering where solutions need to become part of our core product. Over time, repetitive operational work should decrease while your focus on Seller Performance, Procurement strategy, automation and product improvements grows. 📍 Location This is a position based in Hamburg , where you will work closely with our Sales, Product and Engineering team as well as directly with our CEO Christian . Requirements 🚀 Your Impact Ultimately, your work should help xChange transact more containers at better margins , while allowing Procurement to scale without scaling manual work at the same rate. You will: Own and run day-to-day Procurement and tactical Seller Management , using what you learn from operating the processes yourself to continuously improve, streamline and automate the function. Improve our buying economics and Seller Performance by identifying pricing opportunities, negotiating with sellers, driving promotions and improving listing quality, reply speed, release speed and reliability. Use Claude and other tools as part of your day-to-day work to solve problems faster and improve our processes and systems. Build lightweight, bootstrapped solutions yourself when they can solve an immediate problem — from deterministic workflows to agentic solutions. Work closely with Engineering when those solutions need to become more robust, scalable or part of our core product. Build a more systematic, data-driven view of Procurement , so we can identify and prioritize the biggest opportunities across our seller portfolio. Drive larger strategic initiatives such as gatebuy, future pickups and new ways of sourcing inventory that help us build a structurally better trading engine. 🌟 What Makes You a Great Fit? We are looking for someone who combines commercial intuition, strong execution and a product/automation mindset . You are likely a great fit if you: Get genuine satisfaction from negotiating a better deal and spotting commercial opportunities others might miss. Have a passion for trading, pricing and markets — whether that comes from work, the stock market, sports betting or simply how you think. Are commercially confident enough to own seller relationships, make decisions independently and push back when needed . Perform well under pressure and at speed — matching the pace of Sales without sacrificing accuracy. Are highly structured and operationally reliable: fast without becoming sloppy . Enjoy getting your hands dirty and executing the work yourself. Think beyond individual cases and naturally ask how a process can be improved at a system level . Can balance short-term execution with long-term improvement — improving processes, automation and scalability over time. Are data-driven and comfortable using metrics to identify opportunities. Already use AI to solve real-world problems and are excited about building prototypes, workflows and automations. Can translate a business problem into something Engineering can work with. Have strong ownership, drive and the learning velocity to grow further into product and automation . You do not need to be a software engineer . We care much more about your ability to understand a problem deeply, imagine a better solution, prototype where possible and collaborate effectively with Engineers. Deep container knowledge and traditional Procurement experience are also not prerequisites . This role might not be for you if… You prefer having perfect information before making decisions — this role requires fast judgment under uncertainty . You don’t enjoy working in a high-pressure, fast-moving commercial environment where Procurement needs to match the pace of Sales. You prefer staying at one level of the problem rather than switching between what needs to happen now, what needs to change commercially, and what needs to improve in the process or product . You prefer clearly bounded responsibilities over end-to-end ownership — we expect you to take decisions, push back on sellers when needed, and stay accountable until the issue is actually resolved. 👀 What to Expect A rare combination of commercial and product ownership: You will understand and improve the full Procurement system — from the economics of individual trades to the processes and technology behind the function. A role that evolves with you: You will initially spend significant time running Procurement hands-on. As you improve and automate the function, your role should increasingly shift toward Seller Performance, Procurement economics, product and automation. Direct exposure to the business: You will work closely with our CEO Christian and have direct visibility into how supply, pricing and seller performance translate into containers transacted and margin. Build rather than inherit: You are not joining a mature Procurement function with a fixed playbook. You will help define how Procurement at xChange should work in the future, from how we manage sellers today to how much of the function can eventually be automated. AI as a real working tool: We expect you to use tools such as Claude to increase your own leverage and continuously challenge which parts of your job still need to be done manually. The long-term opportunity is to help build a Procurement engine that becomes one of xChange’s core competitive advantages . ** Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow
